title: Beginner Home Workout for Women (20 Minutes, No Equipment)
intro: This 20-minute routine suits women and mummies who are just starting out. All you need is the floor and a chair. The focus is building strength across your whole body so daily tasks, carrying your kids and climbing stairs feel easier.
muscles: Glutes, thighs, core, chest, shoulders and arms. A full-body strength workout, not just one area.
steps: Warm up for 3 minutes: march on the spot, roll your shoulders and hips.
Glute bridge 12 times, then squat to a chair 10 times.
Wall push-ups or knee push-ups 8-10 times.
Reverse lunges while holding a chair, 8 times on each leg.
Rest 1 minute, repeat for 3 rounds, then stretch for 2 minutes.
mistakes: Avoiding strength training because you're afraid of getting bulky. Muscle helps your body look more toned, not bulky.
Holding your breath while moving. Breathe out during the hardest part.
Doing too much in the first week until you're sore for a week and then quit.
easier: Do just 2 rounds and fewer reps. Use a higher chair for squats and do push-ups against the wall.
harder: Add more reps, lower slowly over 3 seconds, switch from knee push-ups to full push-ups, and try single-leg glute bridges.
dose: 2-3 rounds, 3 times a week with a rest day in between. On other days, walk for 20-30 minutes if you have time.
safety: If you've just given birth or are pregnant, get your doctor's clearance first. See a physio if you have urine leakage, a bulge in the middle of your tummy during exercise, or ongoing back pain.

faq.q: Will strength training make women bulky?
faq.a: It's not that easy. Most women will look more toned and feel stronger. Big muscles need years of heavy training with a specific diet.

faq.q: Can this workout slim down my tummy, arms and thighs?
faq.a: We understand that's what many people want. But fat can't be removed from just one spot. This workout strengthens your muscles, and when your eating and daily movement are under control, fat will come off from your whole body at your body's own pace.

faq.q: Can I work out during my period?
faq.a: Yes, if you feel comfortable. Many find light exercise helps reduce bloating and cramps. If you're tired, do fewer rounds or just go for a walk.
